sections.html:
Englewood sits just south of Denver in the South Platte valley, in the western part of Arapahoe County. The city is small, about 6.6 square miles, and stands 5,348 feet above sea level. People per square mile numbered 5,127 in 2020. The census that year found 33,659 residents (30,255 in 2010), and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 35,305.

Households average 2.01 people, and 49.2% of homes are lived in by their owners. For 2020 to 2024 the median owner-occupied value was $572,900 and median gross rent was $1,668. So Englewood sellers include owners of small houses and condos along with landlords. Take the median as a loose reference. It says little about your particular property.

Broadway and Hampden Avenue cut the city into four quadrants, each with its own character.

  • Northwest: the oldest part, holding downtown, City Center and houses dating to the 1910s. A former General Iron site awaits redevelopment.
  • Southwest: newer housing next to many industrial facilities, plus Belleview Park.
  • Southeast: nearly all residential, newer than the north and southwest, running to the Highline Canal.
  • Northeast: the hospital campus with Swedish Medical Center and Craig Hospital.

Hampden Hills is the city's newest and wealthiest area and includes many apartment complexes. Since house age differs so much between quadrants, buyers and their inspectors will ask about the age of the furnace, roof and plumbing. Have the answers ready.

Englewood skews older, with 15.0% of residents 65 or over, and 80.7% of people were in the same house a year earlier. That pattern means a steady flow of estates and downsizing sales. Out-of-state heirs who inherit a house often prefer a clean sale to managing repairs from afar.

Englewood property is taxed by Arapahoe County on the state calendar, which Colorado statute 39-10-104.5 sets.

Payment optionDue dateRule
First halfOn or before the last day of FebruaryInstallments under $25 cannot be split
Second halfJune 15Late amounts accrue 1% interest per month
Single paymentOn or before the last day of AprilSmall bills must be paid in full by April 30

Late amounts collect 1% a month, and even a few days into a month are charged as the whole month. To confirm the current rule and your own balance, call the Arapahoe County Treasurer.

Your share of the current year's tax, through the closing date, is calculated by the title company. Older unpaid taxes have to be cleared before the deed transfers cleanly. Request a payoff number early from the Treasurer or the title company, and a balance will not catch you off guard at the table.

Operators in Englewood need two licenses: a city sales and use tax license and a short-term rental license. In residential zones the operator must be the primary resident, living on the property at least 185 days a year.

  • Applications require a current deed on file with Arapahoe County, a notarized residency affidavit and two proofs of primary residence in residential zones.
  • Insurance must include at least $1 million in personal liability coverage.
  • Parking means one permanent space for each rented bedroom, and no more than two on the street.
  • Fees went up January 1, 2026: $600 for a new application, $400 for a renewal, plus $75 for inspection and $200 at issuance.

If a house cannot meet these conditions, a buyer who intended to rent it nightly may pay less, so check the license status before pricing.

Most of the city belongs to Englewood Public Schools, and small portions fall in Littleton Public Schools and Sheridan Public Schools. RTD's D Line stops at Englewood Station in the Civic Center, and commuters averaged 22.6 minutes to work for 2020 to 2024. The climate is drier than much of the Front Range at 10.42 inches a year, though the temperature swings are still hard on roofs and exterior finishes.

Did you run the house as a short-term rental? A buyer will want proof that both licenses were in place and that you met the residency rule. Keep both licenses, the residency affidavit and the insurance papers together in one folder. A house that cannot meet today's conditions is worth less to someone who wanted nightly income, and the price should reflect that. A buyer who wants to live in it or rent it long term cares much less.

sections.h2: Inherited houses and heirs who live far away
sections.html:
An estate is one of the commonest reasons for a fast sale in this city. Heirs live elsewhere, and an unfinished repair or aging furnace turns into a monthly worry. Collect the papers showing who can sign, then give the title company every name on the list. It can explain what else it needs and how a signing works for someone out of state.

Choosing a cash buyer spares the family repairs, showings and the expense of maintaining the property while paperwork moves along.

sections.h2: What to bring to the title company
sections.html:
Pull together your latest Arapahoe County tax statement, loan payoff details if the house is mortgaged, and the deed or a list of every owner on it. For a former rental, add the licenses and the insurance papers. For an estate, add whatever shows who has authority to sign. A short folder like this lets the title company begin its search the day you accept an offer, and it cuts the number of back-and-forth calls.

If something is missing, say so on the first call. Most items can be tracked down while the rest of the sale moves ahead.

sections.h2: How do you sell an Englewood house fast?
sections.html:
Options are an agent listing, a sale on your own, or a cash purchase. A listing may fetch the top price for a house in good shape. Cash moves faster when a house needs work, has tenants or belongs to an estate.

The state documentary fee on a deed is $0.01 per $100 of consideration over $500. We buy houses in Englewood and nearby Arapahoe County in any condition. Describe the property and we will respond. A no from you costs nothing.

sections.h2: Steps in an Englewood cash sale
sections.html:
1. Tell us about the property and its condition.
  2. We review the details and write an offer.
  3. On acceptance, the title company runs a search, asks the Arapahoe County Treasurer about taxes and prepares the deed.
  4. You pick a closing date and sign.
  5. The county records the deed and the money goes to you.

An offer commits you to nothing. Set it beside a listing and walk away if it does not fit.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Englewood?
faqs.a: Census data for 2020 to 2024 gives $572,900 as the median value of owner-occupied homes. Treat it as a benchmark, because each house differs.
Arapahoe County. That is where Englewood deeds are recorded and property taxes are billed.

faqs.q: Do I need a license for an Airbnb in Englewood?
faqs.a: Yes, two: a city sales and use tax license and a short-term rental license. In residential zones you must also live at the property at least 185 days a year.

faqs.q: When are Colorado property taxes due for an Englewood house?
faqs.a: State law allows two halves, due by the last day of February and by June 15, or one payment by the last day of April.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Englewood house with an unfinished repair?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer takes the house as it stands, so unfinished work does not have to be completed before closing.
